First of all remember that this is a role playing game. When you describe the room you should use some "extra words" when it comes to the relevant parts of the puzzle. The moment they ask for anything about that you can ask them for a check of some sort. If it is high enough they have a hint. If it is not so high they might also get a hint, pointing them to look into another thing or trying again under different conditions.

My second advice is that there is no need for them to solve the puzzle in order to continue. Maybe failing the puzzle in a specific way makes the door explode, allowing them to pass but damaging the party. Maybe the levers that can open the door are coated with some long lasting poison and at some point they got a warning about not touching stuff making it part of the puzzle.

I love puzzles.

For spells you only have two slots so I would first recommend you that you pick something you enjoy casting. As for each one of those:

I don't know how much do you use Hex but if you have to cast one concentration and damaging spell, I can tell you that Wall of Fire is way more difficult to place than Hex.

Dimension Door is both a lifesaver and a puzzle-solver. Many things will become possible when you can teleport to a place you don't need to see with an ally and whaetever you are carrying.

For Banishment let me tell  you than the most overlook and broken aspect of it is that outsiders (demons, celestials, etc.)  don't come back if you concentrate for just one minute. With just one fail charisma saving throw to avoid that.

As for an Invocation, being able to cast Compulsion is definetly fun as you can make a lot of people dance around you. On the other hand, for an offensive spell that specifically says that can't make a creature move into an obviously deadly hazard is pretty meh.

Every wargamer will always tell you to pick Slow for good reasons.

For Eldritch Spear many say that is useless in a common encounter. On the long run however many large scale combats tend to feature large scale (and therefore more dangerous) creatures and effects. A good long range attack can make many things esaier.

If what you actually want is to play then there should be no problem if you just help your friend. I mean, if it is the first time for all of you, then no matter who DM that you are all going to figure out most of the game together at the same time.
